project.title: Pepsi "Crave"
project.format: Global beverage campaign centered on a 30-second hero film and a reusable liquid-footage asset library for regional content

why: A strong campaign-visual reference because the BUCK case is not just a polished one-off film. It documents a campaign system built from practical liquid shots, motion-control capture, and swappable pack assets that Pepsi teams could reuse across markets. That makes it useful for studying how a sensory hero concept can become a modular global rollout kit rather than a single locked edit.

artDirection.title: Practical cola physics become the campaign's main character
artDirection.study: BUCK frames propelled cola, splashes, bubbles, and impact moments as the visual star of the campaign, using custom rigs and motion-control capture so the product sensation reads before copy does.
artDirection.reuse: When the product promise is visceral, build the campaign around one physical behavior viewers can feel immediately instead of surrounding the pack with unrelated lifestyle scenes.

artDirection.title: Condensation, ice, and tight pack crops sell thirst at speed
artDirection.study: The case repeatedly emphasizes close, high-detail shots of cans and bottles with condensation intact, paired with flashes of humanity only where they intensify the anticipation arc.
artDirection.reuse: Use macro product framing when the campaign needs to communicate appetite or texture instantly on large screens and in short edits.

artDirection.title: The hero film is designed from a reusable shot kit
artDirection.study: Rather than producing a fixed hero film first and repurposing it later, BUCK describes building a library of multi-functional cola shots that could serve both the flagship spot and downstream regional content.
artDirection.reuse: Plan the asset library before the master edit when global teams will need many derivatives from one expensive production shoot.

channelFormats.title: Thirty-second flagship film
channelFormats.notes: The campaign's anchor is a short hero film that moves through anticipation, impact, and satisfaction using high-speed liquid moments and quick flashes of humanity.
channelFormats.cropSystem: Compose shots with enough negative space and isolated action that the same footage can be reframed for multiple aspect ratios without losing the product read.
channelFormats.reuse: Build the hero film from shots that can survive extraction, not only from transitions that work in one locked timeline.

channelFormats.title: Global teams receive swap-ready campaign assets
channelFormats.notes: BUCK states that Pepsi needed the footage to work for teams across the globe, with cans and bottles flexible enough to swap logos while preserving ice and condensation.
channelFormats.cropSystem: Keep brand marks, pack silhouettes, and liquid motion separated enough in comp that localized branding can change without reshooting the whole sequence.
channelFormats.reuse: If a campaign must scale internationally, bake localization flexibility into the source footage and compositing plan from day one.

assets.notes: Custom-shot liquid footage provides the campaign's core emotional and visual payoff, functioning as both a cinematic centerpiece and modular raw material.
assets.reuse: Invest in a few unforgettable physical captures when the product's appeal depends on texture, force, or refreshment.

assets.notes: Pack shots are built to support logo replacement while maintaining consistent ice, condensation, and appetite cues.
assets.reuse: Separate product realism from market-specific branding so the same campaign base can travel globally.

assets.notes: The preserved wet surface treatment keeps every derivative asset feeling cold and tactile even after brand swapping and recropping.
assets.reuse: Treat surface detail as a system requirement, not just a finishing flourish, when the campaign is selling refreshment.

motion.title: High-speed motion control turns refreshment into spectacle
motion.notes: The moving image language depends on slow-motion collisions, splashes, and propelled liquid events captured through specialized rigs and cameras.
motion.fallback: If this level of production is unavailable, keep the same appetite logic through fewer but sharper practical shots instead of replacing everything with generic CG motion.

motion.title: Motion follows a clear crave-to-satisfaction progression
motion.notes: BUCK describes an emotional arc of crave, consumption, and satisfaction, which makes the edit feel like a campaign story rather than a disconnected reel of pretty liquid shots.
motion.fallback: Even in short cutdowns, preserve a simple tension-release sequence so the motion still communicates a product feeling.

implementation.format: Global beverage campaign system built from hero-film footage, localization-ready packshots, and downstream regional derivatives
implementation.notes: This is strong enough for accepted status because the first-party BUCK case explicitly covers the campaign's purpose, the reusable shot-library strategy, the motion-control production method, and the global adaptation requirement. It offers enough evidence to study campaign asset modularity without copying Pepsi-owned visuals.
